facts.claim: Langflow issue #1864 exists, is open, was opened 2024-05-08, and requests role-based access control, sharing grants and per-user read/edit permissions for flows
Issue #1864 shows no linked PRs or branches under Development, so no merged or open PR is visible for it
Langflow v1.12.6 release exists (dated 13 October) and its notes contain no access-control, roles, sharing, permissions or audit items

Upstream Langflow docs already describe an authorization model: pluggable RBAC over flows, projects, deployments, files, variables, knowledge bases, shares, roles, teams and an audit log, with built-in roles viewer, developer and admin (not owner/editor/viewer)

Open-source Langflow registers a pass-through authorization service that allows everything; enforcement needs a separate plugin, and OSS includes no registered plugin; the flag LANGFLOW_AUTHZ_ENABLED defaults to false
The upstream docs link no reference plugin or source code, and do not say which version introduced authorization
Repository is MIT licensed (spdx MIT from GitHub API)
Backend test-file count of 2480 and 957 open PRs were checked against the repo
A later upstream release or PR implements the owner/editor/viewer roles with per-flow and per-folder grants as specified in the seed

full_card.provenance: Real: langflow-ai/langflow MIT, pinned v1.12.6; feature issue #1864 open since 2024-05-08.

Build.why: Reference plus hidden multi-user matrices estimated 3-5 days.

spike_plan.kill_if: Dependency install needs network at run time, or a later upstream release ships a working owner/editor/viewer enforcement the snapshot could be read against (then re-scope or seal harder), or the endpoint surface cannot be split into buckets.
spike_plan.pass_if: Existing backend suite runs offline-capable and deterministic; endpoint count supports at least 4 partial-credit families; spike route enforcement passes deterministically.
steps: In a throwaway networked container, clone langflow at tag v1.12.6 and install backend deps offline-capable (record install time and any failures); run the existing backend tests once and record the pass count and time.

Check whether the 1.13 line (or any later tag) contains an authorization plugin or the roles/shares tables: inspect tags and release artifacts for the authz seam only, not the implementation, and record what is public.
Count flow, folder, component, variable, MCP, websocket and export endpoints in the snapshot to size the endpoint families for partial-credit buckets.
Write a minimal model-only spike: roles table plus one per-flow grant check on flow GET and PATCH, and confirm the existing suite still passes.
Run a two-user allow/deny pytest on that route three times to confirm determinism.

v1.summary: The seed is real and mostly well-grounded: issue #1864 is open with no linked PR, and v1.12.6 has no access-control work, but upstream authorization docs already outline a near-identical model (roles, shares, audit, plugin seam) under different role names, so lookup is partial and sealing depends on keeping the reference and hidden tests ours. Validated with 8 h tier and est. 10 frontier hours; not killed, but the spike must confirm offline dependency install and check that no later upstream release ships enforcement code.

v2.note: The grading is hand-rolled multi-user matrices tied to an API we invent ourselves: owner/editor/viewer roles, the shape of the audit endpoint and the grant semantics. Any other reasonable design would fail. Upstream docs already describe a pluggable authz seam with viewer/developer/admin roles, so this spec conflicts with the maintainers' direction and fails the realism check. The frontier estimate of 10 h exceeds the 8 h tier, and the reference is unwritten. The BaxBench backend family is a neighbour at 0.19.
